headline: Public speakers urged council to pause Flock cameras; council leaders said they would talk with incoming administration.
summary: Speakers said the cameras were installed without public input and keep vehicle data indefinitely, and asked the city to report how many crimes they helped solve. Three letters to public works and police about speeding on Rice Street were approved. The council also approved a change to the circus and carnival rules, requiring a charity to be named in the permit application. Two pothole claims, $275 and $300, were approved, and a $1,349.08 tire claim was denied.
decisions: Approved the amendment to Chapter 167, Circus and Carnivals, 3-0.
Approved liquor license renewals after a public hearing, with one member recused.
Continued the Isla Express license application at 584 Smithfield Avenue until the first meeting in December.
Approved sending three letters to public works and police about Rice Street speeding and crosswalks.
Approved sending a letter to public works about Roosevelt Avenue traffic and a traffic study.
Approved six Rhode Island Energy pole petitions, pending the Public Works director's approval.
Confirmed Michael William Cooper to the Juvenile Hearing Board, 6-0.
Denied the $1,349.08 tire damage claim from Pericles Vieira and referred it to Vinagro, 6-0.
Approved the $275 pothole claim for Napoleon Gonzales and the $300 pothole claim for Nicholas Jensen, 6-0.
discussion: Flock cameras: Public speakers said the cameras record every passing vehicle and urged the council to pause the program. Council leaders said they would talk with the incoming administration, and with any new police or public safety leaders.

Rice Street traffic: Public speakers said cars speed and run stop signs on Rice Street, and that two cars flipped over in recent months. The letters seek stop-ahead signs, a crosswalk status, and a 60-day response on a one-way route from Benefit to Cottage.

School zone speed cameras: A public speaker asked the council for a full, independent audit of the program. The speaker said $50 tickets and tax refund offsets hurt families, and asked whether the cameras are making kids safer.

Teacher contract: A public speaker said no Finance Committee meeting was scheduled on the contract between the Pawtucket School Committee and the Pawtucket Teachers' Alliance. The speaker asked the council to move it to a full council vote.
Circus and carnival rules: Members said the charity should be named when the permit is applied for, not afterward. They said the ordinance should not set a donation percentage.
